raw_case_text:
A 36 years old Filipino woman domestic helper who had been working in Singapore for the past 2 years presented to the Accident and Emergency Medicine Department with a 10-day history of non-bloody diarrhoea, abdominal distension, altered mental state and fever. Prior to her admission she had a history of chronic abdominal pain with altered bowel habits which was treated symptomatically by her general practitioner. The patient was from a rural village in the Philippines and frequently ate pork liver prepared in vinegar, a Filipino dish "Kilawin" which includes raw fish, shellfish, and half-cooked meat mixed with vinegar and Ilocano delicacies "Papaitan, Isaw and Igado" which contain pig intestines.
She was initially admitted with the diagnosis of gastroenteritis. However, her condition deteriorated with worsening abdominal pain and distension. An urgent surgical consult was sought following a computed tomography scan of the abdomen and pelvis which demonstrated grossly dilated colon suspicious for toxic megacolon with possible worm infestation of the small bowel (Fig. 1, Figs. 2-4). Her lab results on admission showed an elevated white cell count (14.6 x 103/uL) with elevated C-reactive protein levels at 288.1 mg/L. Clinically, she was septic with signs of generalised peritonitis.
An emergent laparotomy performed revealed grossly dilated colon with numerous areas of ulceration and perforation resulting in faeculant peritonitis. A total colectomy was performed and during the transection of small bowel, segments of an adult tapeworm was retrieved (Fig. 5). As she was haemodynamically unstable on dual vasopressors with areas of small bowel ischaemia, decision was made for temporary abdominal closure. She subsequently underwent a relook laparotomy where a 2nd adult tapeworm was retrieved. As her rectal mucosa was ulcerated, an end ileostomy was formed.
She was commenced on IV metronidazole and oral albendazole and praziquantel. A Computed tomography scan of the brain was also performed in view of her history of altered mental state, but this did not reveal intracerebral lesions to suggest parasitosis or neurocysticerosis. She made a full recovery and was able to return to the Philippines.
Histopathology analysis of the total colectomy specimen showed there was fulminant amoebic (Entamoeba histolytica) colitis resulting in ulceration and perforation of the colon. In the specimens, co-helminthic infection with Trichuris trichuira nematodes and Taenium solium cestodes were also found.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 36-year-old Filipino female domestic helper presented in Singapore with a 10-day history of non-bloody diarrhea, abdominal distension, fever, and altered mental status.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented to the emergency department with 10 days of watery non-bloody diarrhea, progressive abdominal distension, fever, and altered mental status, superimposed on a prior history of chronic abdominal pain and altered bowel habits treated symptomatically by her general practitioner. After initial admission for presumed gastroenteritis, her abdominal pain and distension rapidly worsened with clinical sepsis and generalized peritonitis.
subjective.past_medical_history: History of chronic abdominal pain and altered bowel habits. Originally from a rural village in the Philippines, working as a domestic helper in Singapore for 2 years; dietary history significant for frequent consumption of raw/undercooked Filipino dishes including pork liver in vinegar, 'Kilawin' (raw fish, shellfish, and half-cooked meat in vinegar), and Ilocano delicacies ('Papaitan', 'Isaw', and 'Igado') containing pig intestines.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for 10-day non-bloody diarrhea, worsening abdominal pain and distension, fever, and altered mental status.

objective.physical_examination: Clinically septic with fever, altered mental status, gross abdominal distension, and signs of generalized peritonitis.
objective.routine_investigations: Admission laboratory tests showed leukocytosis (WBC 14.6 x 10^3/uL) and markedly elevated C-reactive protein (CRP 288.1 mg/L).
objective.advanced_workup: CT of the abdomen and pelvis demonstrated a grossly dilated colon suspicious for toxic megacolon and intraluminal ribbon-like structures suggestive of small bowel helminthic infestation. Non-contrast CT of the brain (performed for altered mental status) was negative for intracerebral lesions or neurocysticercosis. Emergency exploratory laparotomy and subsequent relook laparotomy revealed feculent peritonitis, a grossly dilated colon with multiple transmural ulcerations and perforations, small bowel patchy ischemia, rectal mucosal ulcerations, and two adult tapeworms retrieved from the transected small bowel; total colectomy with temporary abdominal closure followed by end ileostomy formation was performed.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Histopathological analysis of the total colectomy specimen coupled with intraoperative parasite retrieval confirmed fulminant perforating amoebic colitis (Entamoeba histolytica) with feculent peritonitis and triple intestinal parasitic co-infection involving Taenia solium cestodes and Trichuris trichiura nematodes (without neurocysticercosis on brain CT). The patient underwent emergency total colectomy, relook laparotomy with retrieval of two adult tapeworms and end ileostomy creation, dual-vasopressor ICU support, intravenous metronidazole, and oral albendazole and praziquantel. She achieved a full recovery and returned home to the Philippines.
